era: 1492 DR — the winter after one of the Gate's own defenders took the Netherbrain's place. The Absolute war ended not with the brain's death but with its leash changing hands: a hero who carried a tadpole accepted ceremorphosis and the brain's power to end the slaughter, and now a vast illithid intellect holds the freed minds of the Sword Coast in check from the shadows. The old Chosen (Ketheric Thorm, Gortash, Orin) are still dead. Keep the timeline straight: the city was saved, but its savior is no longer human, and what it wants next is the open question of the age. Do not raise the long-dead or pre-empt events that haven't happened.
premise: It is the winter after the Battle of Baldur's Gate. The Cult of the Absolute is broken and its three Chosen (Ketheric Thorm, Enver Gortash, Orin the Red) are dead — but the Netherbrain was not destroyed. To end the ceremorphosis cascade, one of the Gate's own defenders took the brain's throne, and a vast illithid intellect now holds every freed mind on the Sword Coast in check from the shadows — a guardian, so far, that no one is sure they trust.
premise_suffix: Here the brain was not destroyed — it was claimed. To end the ceremorphosis cascade, one of the Gate's defenders submitted to the tadpole and took the Netherbrain's throne, becoming an Elder Brain that holds every freed mind on the Coast from spilling into chaos. The city was spared mass transformation. But its salvation now thinks with an alien mind, and the tadpole-touched can feel it at the edge of sleep — a benevolence no one is sure they trust. Into a Gate ruled, in secret, by a mind it cannot see, the player steps: a nobody whose thoughts, for the first time in history, might not be entirely their own.
standing_threads: The watching mind: an Elder Brain born of a former hero holds the Coast's freed minds in check — and every tadpole-survivor can feel its quiet weight; some call it guardian, some call it the next tyrant, and no one can prove which.

The cult reborn upward: scattered Absolute remnants now whisper that the new brain is the true Absolute at last, and gather to serve it — wanted or not — while the Gate's powers debate whether to thank it or destroy it.
Free will on a leash: a resistance of mages, githyanki, and frightened patriars searches for a way to sever the brain's hold without unleashing the cascade it prevents — a knot with no clean cut.
history_append: The crown accepted: at the climax of the Battle of Baldur's Gate, a tadpole-bearing defender chose ceremorphosis over annihilation — taking the Netherbrain's power to halt the mass transformation that would otherwise have swept the Coast.

The new Absolute: the freed minds did not scatter into madness; they were caught and held by the ascended hero-turned-Elder-Brain, which now anchors every former true soul from the dark of the Underdark.

The benevolent unknown: the brain has, so far, used its dominion to protect rather than enslave — but its mind is illithid now, its timescale geological, and the Gate lives under a guardian whose mercy is a daily, unprovable gamble.
story_seeds_append: A tadpole-survivor begins receiving precise, helpful 'intuitions' that save lives — and then one that asks something terrible in return; the party must decide whether the watching mind is to be obeyed, refused, or hunted.
An Absolute remnant has located what they believe is the brain's physical anchor and means to either worship it or detonate it; both outcomes free the cascade the brain holds back.
A resistance cell offers the party a device that can shield a mind from the brain's reach — but field-testing it on a willing survivor risks cutting them loose from the one thing keeping them sane.

npc-jaheira.where: the Harper safehouses, organizing the resistance
npc-jaheira.note: Refuses to live under any mind but her own; the steadiest hand in the effort to sever the brain's hold without dooming the Coast.

npc-minsc.where: the Gate, ready to 'go for the eyes' of a brain he cannot see
npc-minsc.note: Hates an enemy he can't punch; a blunt, loyal ally to anyone fighting the leash — though Boo, he insists, trusts no one's thoughts but his own.

npc-astarion.where: the Outer City, well away from the brain's true souls
npc-astarion.note: Survived a life of being someone's instrument and has no intention of being a mind's; sells information about the cult-reborn to whoever pays.

npc-shadowheart.note: The brain's bargain — safety for surrender — cuts at her oldest wound; her presence raises the question of whether mercy without choice is mercy at all.

npc-wyll.status: alive, the Blade against a new tyranny
npc-wyll.note: Sees the watching mind as exactly the kind of power his oath was meant to break; torn, as ever, between his city and the harder road.

npc-karlach.where: the front of any fight against the cult-reborn
npc-karlach.note: Will not be told what to feel by anything, least of all an Elder Brain; the loudest 'no' in the city.

npc-the-emperor.note: The mind flayer that once steered the Absolute now watches another wear the crown it understood; whether it means to serve, supplant, or sever the new brain is its own cold calculus.

npc-withers.where: where minds are lost and kept
npc-withers.note: Keeps his ledger of souls; notes, drily, that the new brain has complicated his accounting considerably.

Gale.status: alive — and the resistance's brightest hope (or its gravest temptation)
Gale.where: Sorcerous Sundries, studying the brain's nature
Gale.note: Knows more than anyone about Netherese power and ceremorphosis; the obvious person to find the cut — and the obvious person to be tempted by the crown himself.

Lae'zel.status: alive, blade drawn against the brain
Lae'zel.where: leading gith hunters who will not abide a living Elder Brain
Lae'zel.note: To the githyanki an Elder Brain is the oldest enemy regardless of its mercy; a ruthless, uncompromising ally against it.

Halsin.where: the wilds, watching nature's reaction to the brain
Halsin.note: Feels the watching mind press on the living world itself; a druid's read on whether the brain's 'order' is balance or a slow strangling.

arc_gates.note: Sever the Elder Brain's hold — the Emperor wants the leash cut, ostensibly to free the Coast's minds, in truth so no other intellect outranks its own. Earning its regard unlocks the route to the brain's anchor.

agenda.note: The moment the party holds the means to the brain's throne, the brain's whisper wins: the Emperor turns — not from malice but from appetite — it would sooner wear the crown itself than see it broken, and it strikes to take what's in hand.
